title: NSGo game playtest (version 1)
description: Config is the root of a versioned playtest.yaml document describing the scope, seeded runs, bot profile and measured metrics with goals.

version.description: Version is the schema version; it must equal CurrentVersion (1).

scope.description: Scope identifies the project and scene this playtest exercises.

runs.description: Runs configures the batch of headless seeded runs.

bot.description: Bot selects the bot profile and configures its behavior parameters.

metrics.description: Metrics declares each measured metric, how it is aggregated, and its optional goal.

baselines.description: Baselines declares the reference, degraded and idle outcome policies.

Baselines.description: Baselines declares the outcome policies a playtest expects from its reference bot, a degraded copy of it, and no input at all.

idle.description: Idle declares what a run with no input must reach, and how soon.

reference.description: Reference declares the minimum win rate of the configured bot across the declared seeds.

degraded.description: Degraded declares how the configured bot is weakened and how far below the reference its win rate must stay.

BotConfig.description: BotConfig configures the bot profile and parameters driving input during playtest runs.

profile.description: Profile names the bot profile, such as "platformer-runner", "topdown-explorer", "shooter", "puzzle-solver" or "card-ai".

strategy.description: Strategy is an optional one-line summary of the bot's behavior for reports.

reactionMin.description: ReactionMin is the minimum human reaction jitter duration, such as "120ms".

reactionMax.description: ReactionMax is the maximum human reaction jitter duration, such as "220ms".

params.description: Params holds optional profile-specific scalar parameters (booleans, finite numbers or strings).

DegradedBaseline.description: DegradedBaseline declares a weakened copy of the configured bot and the win-rate limit it must stay under.

reactionScale.description: ReactionScale multiplies the bot's reactionMin and reactionMax, such as 2 for half-speed reactions; set it, DropRate, or both.

dropRate.description: DropRate is the share of the bot's actions discarded, chosen from the run's seed, from 0 to 1.

maxWinRate.description: MaxWinRate is the highest win rate the degraded bot may reach, from 0 to 1; set it, Margin, or both.

margin.description: Margin is the minimum gap between the reference win rate and the degraded win rate, from 0 to 1.

Goal.description: Goal defines the target range or threshold for a Metric and the file the goal comes from.

summary.description: Summary is an optional human-readable description of the goal, such as "most first-timers clear floor 1".

source.description: Source names the file this goal comes from, such as "brief.yaml", "game.yaml" or "playtest.yaml".

min.description: Min is the inclusive lower bound (value >= Min).

max.description: Max is the inclusive upper bound (value <= Max).

IdleBaseline.description: IdleBaseline declares the outcome a run with no input must reach within a simulated duration.

outcome.description: Outcome is the result the idle run must reach: "lose" or "stall".

within.description: Within is the simulated time the idle run may take to reach Outcome, such as "20s"; at most the run's maxDuration (60s when unset).

Measure.description: Measure specifies which telemetry signal a Metric reads and how per-run values combine.

kind.description: Kind selects the telemetry source: "event", "counter", "timer", "outcome", "ratio" or "perf".

key.description: Key names the event kind, counter name, timer name, outcome name or perf field to read.

denomKey.description: DenomKey names the denominator counter for "ratio" metrics (required when Kind is "ratio").

aggregate.description: Aggregate chooses how per-run values combine: "count", "sum", "mean", "median", "min", "max", "p95", "p99" or "rate".

heatMap.description: HeatMap records positioned event coordinates for this metric in the report's heatMaps section.

Metric.description: Metric defines one measured playtest metric, how it is computed across runs, and its optional goal.

name.description: Name uniquely identifies the metric, such as "finished", "median_time" or "frame_time".

label.description: Label is an optional human-readable display name, such as "Finished".

unit.description: Unit is an optional display unit, such as "s", "ms", "%" or "runs".

measure.description: Measure specifies how per-run telemetry is read and aggregated across runs.

goal.description: Goal is the optional target threshold or range this metric is checked against.

ReferenceBaseline.description: ReferenceBaseline declares the minimum win rate of the configured bot.

winRate.description: WinRate is the minimum share of seeded runs the configured bot must win, from 0 to 1.

Runs.description: Runs configures how many seeded runs execute, their seeds, fixed step rate, speed and simulated time limit.

count.description: Count is the number of seeded runs to execute; when 0 and Seeds is non-empty, it defaults to len(Seeds).

seeds.description: Seeds lists explicit per-run random seeds; when fewer than Count, additional seeds are derived sequentially from SeedStart.

seedStart.description: SeedStart is the starting seed used when generating sequential seeds (defaults to 1 when 0).

rate.description: Rate is the fixed simulation step rate in steps per second (defaults to 60 when 0).

speed.description: Speed is the simulation speed multiplier metadata, such as 1 or 8 for 8x speed (defaults to 1 when 0).

maxDuration.description: MaxDuration is the simulated time limit per run before timing out, such as "60s" (defaults to 60s when 0).

Scope.description: Scope identifies the project, scene and optional template a playtest targets.

project.description: Project is the project name or relative path to the project root.

scene.description: Scene names the scene or level the playtest exercises, such as "level_01".

template.description: Template names the template the playtest originated from, such as "platformer2d".
